sections.title: Foundations (Stages 1–2)
sections.description: First computing skills from Stages 1 and 2: spotting computers, following steps and sharing safely.

questions.question: In Scratch, what does a repeat 4 block do to the blocks placed inside it?
questions.options: It runs them once | It runs them 4 times | It makes them run 4 times faster | It deletes them after 4 seconds
questions.explanation: A repeat block is a loop: everything inside it runs again and again, and repeat 4 means it runs exactly 4 times.

questions.question: A programmer adds a comment next to her code. What is the comment for?
questions.options: It makes the program run faster | It is an instruction the computer follows | It fixes bugs by itself | It explains to people what the code does
questions.correctAnswer: It explains to people what the code does
questions.explanation: A comment is a note for people reading the code. The computer skips it — it just helps others understand the program.

questions.question: What is a database?
questions.options: An organised collection of data that is easy to search | A printer that stores paper | A machine that types data for you | A game about sorting numbers
questions.correctAnswer: An organised collection of data that is easy to search
questions.explanation: A database keeps data organised so you can search and sort it quickly — like a well-ordered digital filing cabinet.

questions.question: A database of animal names is sorted from A to Z. Which name comes first?
questions.options: Ant | Zebra | Monkey | Tiger
questions.explanation: Sorting from A to Z puts words in alphabet order. Ant starts with A, so it comes before Monkey, Tiger and Zebra.

questions.question: In a network, what job does a server do?
questions.options: It switches the network off at night | It draws pictures for the other computers | It only plays videos | It stores files and shares them with other computers
questions.correctAnswer: It stores files and shares them with other computers
questions.explanation: A server serves the other computers: it stores files and information and shares them with the clients that ask for them.

questions.question: Which sentence about an Ethernet connection is true?
questions.options: It uses a cable to join a device to a network | It is a kind of printer | It only works outdoors | It is a wireless connection
questions.correctAnswer: It uses a cable to join a device to a network
questions.explanation: Ethernet is a wired connection — a cable plugs the device into the network. Wi-Fi is the wireless way to connect.

questions.question: A program repeats these two steps 4 times: move 100 steps, turn 90 degrees. What shape does it draw?
questions.options: A square | A triangle | A straight line | A circle
questions.explanation: Four equal sides with a quarter turn (90 degrees) at each corner make a square — the loop draws one side each time.

questions.question: What is an algorithm?
questions.options: A set of step-by-step instructions that solves a problem | A kind of computer virus | A place where files are saved | A part of a computer screen
questions.correctAnswer: A set of step-by-step instructions that solves a problem
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a list of clear steps, in order, that solves a problem or gets a job done — like a recipe for the computer.

questions.question: How does a real driverless car decide when to stop?
questions.options: Its sensors and its computer program decide | It simply stops once every minute | A driver hidden inside presses the brakes | Somebody steers it with a TV remote
questions.correctAnswer: Its sensors and its computer program decide
questions.explanation: A driverless car senses the road with cameras and sensors, and its program uses that information to decide what to do — no hidden driver needed.

questions.question: A musician wants the same four notes to play again and again in her program. Which block should she put them inside?
questions.options: A paint block | A stop block | A delete block | A repeat block
questions.explanation: A repeat block plays whatever is inside it over and over — perfect for a tune that uses the same notes again and again.

questions.question: In a database table about pets, one row holds everything about one pet. What is that row called?
questions.options: A record | A file name | A password | A field
questions.explanation: Each row is a record — all the information about one pet. Each column, like Name or Age, is a field.

questions.question: A field in a database is set up to hold only Yes or No. Which answer is allowed in it?
questions.options: Maybe | Yes | Blue | Sometimes
questions.explanation: A Yes/No field accepts exactly two answers: Yes or No. Maybe, Sometimes and Blue do not fit its rule.

questions.question: An inventor designs a gadget: pressing a button makes a light turn on. Which part is the output?
questions.options: The person pressing | The light | The battery | The button
questions.explanation: The output is what the gadget does back to you. The button is the input you press; the light turning on is the output.

questions.question: A cipher moves every letter one step forward, so A becomes B and B becomes C. What happens to the letter Z?
questions.options: It wraps around back to A | Z always stays as Z | The cipher breaks and cannot be used | The message just stops at Z
questions.correctAnswer: It wraps around back to A
questions.explanation: Think of the alphabet as a circle. After Z you go back to the start, so Z wraps around and becomes A.

questions.question: What is a sub-routine in a program?
questions.options: Instructions for one job, written once and used again and again | A mistake the programmer made | The screen where the game is played | A list of the players in a game
questions.correctAnswer: Instructions for one job, written once and used again and again
questions.explanation: A sub-routine is a little set of instructions for one job. You write it once, then use it whenever you need that job done.

questions.question: In Scratch, the y value of a sprite gets bigger. Which way does the sprite move on the screen?
questions.options: Down | It disappears | Up | To the left
questions.explanation: On the Scratch stage, x moves a sprite left and right, and y moves it up and down. A bigger y means higher up the screen.

questions.question: A control system, like a robot vacuum cleaner, follows three steps in order. Which order is correct?
questions.options: Act, think, sense | Sense, think, act | Think, act, sense | Act, sense, think
questions.explanation: First it senses the world with its sensors, then it thinks using its program, and then it acts — like turning away from a wall.

questions.question: Which sentence about hardware and software is true?
questions.options: Hardware is the parts you can touch; software is the programs | A robot has hardware but never any software | Hardware and software are the same thing | Software is the parts you can touch
questions.correctAnswer: Hardware is the parts you can touch; software is the programs
questions.explanation: Hardware is the physical machine — wheels, screens, chips. Software is the programs that tell the hardware what to do.

questions.question: What is the difference between a forever block and a repeat 10 block?
questions.options: They do exactly the same thing | forever never stops, but repeat 10 stops after 10 times | repeat 10 never stops, but forever stops after 10 times | forever only works with sounds
questions.correctAnswer: forever never stops, but repeat 10 stops after 10 times
questions.explanation: Both are loops. A repeat 10 block counts to 10 and then stops; a forever block keeps going until the program is stopped.

questions.question: Two algorithms solve the same problem. One takes 5 steps and the other takes 12. Why is the 5-step one better?
questions.options: It must have more bugs in it | Using more steps always makes an answer better | Shorter algorithms only work on new computers | It is more efficient because it uses fewer steps
questions.correctAnswer: It is more efficient because it uses fewer steps
questions.explanation: An efficient algorithm gets the same job done with fewer steps, so it is quicker and easier to follow.

questions.question: Which of these is an input device?
questions.options: A screen | A speaker | A printer | A keyboard
questions.explanation: An input device sends information into the computer — like typing on a keyboard. Screens, speakers and printers give information out.

questions.question: In an online game, someone you do not know asks for your name and home address. What should you do?
questions.options: Share it to be polite | Share only your home address | Share it if they say they are a child too | Do not share it, and tell a trusted grown-up
questions.correctAnswer: Do not share it, and tell a trusted grown-up
questions.explanation: Your name and address are personal information. Keep them private online, and always tell a trusted grown-up when a stranger asks.

questions.question: A cipher turns the message HELLO into a secret form that others cannot read. What is the secret form called?
questions.options: Ciphertext | A bar chart | Plain text | A search engine
questions.explanation: The ordinary message is called plain text. After the cipher scrambles it, the secret version is called ciphertext.

questions.question: Leyla wants to build a big game. What does it mean to break the task into sub-tasks?
questions.options: Ask the computer to build it by itself | Play other games to copy their ideas | Split the big job into smaller parts and do them one at a time | Delete the game and start again
questions.correctAnswer: Split the big job into smaller parts and do them one at a time
questions.explanation: Breaking a big task into sub-tasks makes it easier: you build one small part at a time until the whole game is finished.

questions.question: In a spreadsheet, what is one little box where a row and a column meet called?
questions.options: A folder | A cell | A sprite | A page
questions.explanation: A spreadsheet is made of rows and columns, and each little box where they meet is a cell. Each cell holds one piece of data.

questions.question: Omar tests his program and it does not do what he planned. What is a mistake in a program called?
questions.options: A server | A virus | A cell | A bug
questions.explanation: A mistake in a program is called a bug, and fixing it is called debugging. Testing helps you find bugs so you can fix them.

questions.question: Which of these is a computer?
questions.options: A paper book | A tablet | A wooden spoon | A woolly sock
questions.explanation: A tablet is a computer: it has a screen, follows programs and responds when you tap it. The others have no computer inside.

questions.question: What does a network let computers do?
questions.options: Cook food for people | Connect to each other and share things | Grow bigger every day | Sleep during the night
questions.correctAnswer: Connect to each other and share things
questions.explanation: A network joins computers together so they can share things with each other, like messages, pictures and files.

questions.question: A sandwich algorithm says: 1 get the bread, 2 add the cheese, 3 eat the sandwich. Which step do you do first?
questions.options: Wash the plate | Add the cheese | Eat the sandwich | Get the bread
questions.explanation: Instructions in an algorithm are followed in order. Step 1 comes first, so you get the bread before anything else.

questions.question: You count the cars that pass your window: 4 red, 2 blue and 1 green. Which colour did you see most?
questions.options: Green | Yellow | Blue | Red
questions.explanation: Compare the counts: 4 is bigger than 2 and 1, so red is the colour you saw most. Counting and comparing is working with data.

questions.question: Which everyday machine has a small computer inside it?
questions.options: A glass of water | A garden stone | A cotton T-shirt | A washing machine
questions.explanation: A washing machine has a small computer that follows a program to wash the clothes. Water, stones and T-shirts have no computer.

questions.question: Which of these is safe to share in an online game?
questions.options: Your home address | Your password | Your full name and school | Your favourite colour
questions.explanation: A favourite colour does not tell strangers who or where you are. Your address, full name, school and password must stay private.
